import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022],
    'Qatar': [81.2, 81.4, 81.6, 81.7, 81.9, 82.1, 82.2, 82.4, 82.5, 82.7, 82.8, 83.0, 83.1],

    'Rwanda': [65.5, 65.8, 66.0, 66.2, 66.4, 66.6, 66.8, 67.0, 67.1, 67.2, 67.3, 67.4, 67.5],
    'Tanzania': [68.0, 68.2, 68.4, 68.6, 68.8, 69.0, 69.2, 69.4, 69.5, 69.6, 69.7, 69.8, 69.9],
    'Tunisia': [77.5, 77.6, 77.7, 77.8, 77.9, 78.0, 78.1, 78.2, 78.3, 78.4, 78.5, 78.6, 78.7],
    'Uruguay': [78.0, 78.1, 78.3, 78.4, 78.5, 78.6, 78.7, 78.8, 78.9, 79.0, 79.1, 79.2, 173.4]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars='Year', var_name='Country', value_name='Survival Rate')

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.lineplot(
    data=df_melted,
    x='Year',
    y='Survival Rate',
    hue='Country',
    palette='husl',
    linewidth=2.5,
    marker='o',
    markersize=8
)

plt.title('Trends in Child Mortality Rates Across Countries (2010-2022)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Life Expectancy at Birth (years)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(df['Year'], rotation=45)
plt.legend(title='Country', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')
===== summary.txt
The chart presented is a line graph illustrating the trends in elderly survival rates for individuals aged 65 and above across six countries from 2010 to 2022. The title of the chart, "Trends in Elderly Survival Rates (65+) Across Countries (2010-2022)," clearly indicates its focus. The x-axis represents the years, spanning from 2010 to 2022, while the y-axis denotes the elderly survival rate as a percentage, ranging from 65% to 83%.

Each country is represented by a distinct colored line, allowing for easy differentiation: Qatar (pink), Romania (brown), Rwanda (green), Tanzania (teal), Tunisia (blue), and Uruguay (purple). Data points along each line are marked with circular indicators, showing the exact survival rates for each year.

Over the observed period, Qatar consistently exhibits the highest elderly survival rates, starting at 81.2% in 2010 and gradually increasing to 83.1% by 2022. Uruguay follows, beginning at 78.0% in 2010 and rising to 79.3% in 2022. Tunisia's survival rate also shows a steady increase from 77.5% to 78.7% over the same period. Romania's survival rates start at 76.0% and climb to 77.2%, reflecting a modest upward trend. Tanzania's rates improve from 68.0% in 2010 to 69.9% in 2022, while Rwanda, beginning with the lowest rate of 65.5%, demonstrates a gradual increase to 67.5% by 2022.

Overall, the chart reveals a positive trend in elderly survival rates across all six countries, with Qatar leading significantly and Rwanda showing the most room for improvement. The consistent upward trajectories suggest advancements in healthcare and living conditions for the elderly population in these nations.
